category.label: Ashwagandha
category.comparisonNote: Root powder, extracts and blends are distinct profiles. Compare material costs within the same formulation; a standardized extract mass is required to calculate withanolides.

guide.title: Ashwagandha: promising short trials, uncertain equivalence
guide.summary: Stress and sleep findings need to be read alongside extract identity, standardization and trial duration.
guide.evidence: Some small randomized trials report improvements in stress measures and sleep with specific preparations.
guide.limitations: Short follow-up, small samples and heterogeneous extracts limit certainty. Results for a standardized root extract do not establish the same benefit for whole root powder or a blend.
guide.catalogReading: Compare the same material class. Withanolide mass can be calculated only when both the standardized extract mass and percentage are verified. A headline milligram figure may represent a different basis.
guide.safety: Liver injury has been reported, and thyroid effects and drug interactions are concerns. Avoid use in pregnancy; seek professional advice for relevant conditions or medicines.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: A swallowed product supplies a mixture of plant constituents; powders and extracts can have different compositions.
Absorption and metabolism depend on the preparation. Human studies do not establish one uniform pathway for all products.
Proposed stress-response mechanisms do not prove a clinical benefit; withanolide percentage is not a measure of cure.
guide.treatment: No established cure for anxiety disorders, insomnia or thyroid disease. Persistent symptoms need assessment rather than self-treatment with an extract.
guide.whoMayBenefit: Some adults seeking short-term stress or sleep support may consider a specific studied preparation after reviewing risks and alternatives.
guide.routineUse: No group should assume it is essential or a lifelong supplement. Long-term safety is uncertain.

whoCanConsider: Adults discussing persistent stress or sleep difficulties and appropriate treatment options with a clinician.
People considering a short-term, clearly identified extract while accepting the limited and formulation-specific evidence.
whoShouldReview: Avoid during pregnancy or breastfeeding; discuss alternatives with a clinician.
Liver or thyroid disease requires particular caution.
Thyroid medicines, sedatives, immunosuppressants, and blood-pressure or diabetes medicines need interaction review.
buyingGuide.foodSummary: Ashwagandha is a botanical preparation with no ordinary food equivalent. Root powder in a food or drink does not establish equivalence to a studied standardized extract.

value.targetedUse: A short-term clinician-reviewed discussion of a specific extract for stress or sleep difficulties.
value.reason: Small studies suggest possible benefit, but preparations vary and long-term safety is uncertain.
worthWhen: The preparation can be compared meaningfully with a studied extract.
Safety, medicines and a plan to reassess use have been reviewed.
skipWhen: There is no defined problem to address.
The purchase is driven by universal stress, hormone or cure claims.
value.scope: Editorial priority for a selected short-term context; it does not replace assessment or establish safety of all extracts.

dos.title: Identify the material
dos.detail: Separate root powder, standardized extract and blends; compare the preparation with the one actually studied.

dos.title: Review safety and ongoing need
dos.detail: Check medicines and relevant conditions, and plan to reassess rather than assume indefinite use.

donts.title: Don't multiply incompatible label values
donts.detail: Calculate withanolides only from verified extract mass and its matching standardization, not total root or blend mass.

donts.title: Don't treat broad claims as evidence
donts.detail: Universal stress, hormone or cure promises do not show that a particular extract is suitable for you.

intakeGuide.summary: No established dietary requirement or universally appropriate extract dose. Trials use particular extracts and standardizations; products are not interchangeable.
notes: No automatic dose increase is assigned for training frequency or experience.

medicalGuide.summary: Condition-specific evidence, separate from sports benefits and purchase priority.

conditions.findings: Small, short trials of selected extracts suggest symptom benefits; they do not establish treatment of an anxiety disorder or chronic insomnia.
conditions.limits: No established cure for anxiety disorders, insomnia or thyroid disease. Persistent symptoms need assessment rather than self-treatment with an extract.

pathway.title: A plant mixture with an incomplete human pathway map
pathway.summary: Ashwagandha contains multiple constituents. Human absorption, metabolites and contributions to reported effects are not mapped as one established pathway.

steps.label: Preparations deliver different constituent mixtures
steps.detail: Root powders and root or leaf extracts contain differing withanolides and other plant compounds.

steps.label: Uptake and processing remain preparation dependent
steps.detail: A product's composition does not establish which constituents or metabolites reach a particular tissue in humans.

steps.label: Multiple proposed actions remain under study
steps.detail: Preclinical mechanisms and small human trials do not establish a single causal route for every preparation or outcome.

pathway.caveat: This is an uncertainty map, not a proven cortisol-lowering or thyroid-treatment pathway. Withanolide percentage alone cannot predict efficacy or safety.
